content.text: {"scene_id":"scene-CATS-19","layout_selection_status":"determined","selected_layouts":[{"layout_code":"TA-33","layout_role":"primary_applicable","source_locator":"TA-33, Figure 6P-33, PDF pages 964-965; SEC-6N.11 paragraph 06, PDF page 887","matched_scene_facts":["One stationary right-lane closure","Multilane divided roadway","Long-term work lasting more than three days","Channelizing devices are used around the closed lane","Urban arterial context is compatible with the multi-lane roadway treatment","Posted speed is 25 mph, which can be used later for TA-33 taper and spacing calculations"],"conflicting_scene_facts":["The full roadway lane count is unknown","The exact work-zone relationship to the signalized intersection is not fully established","Arrow-board deployment is unknown; TA-33's arrow-board requirement is specifically conditional on a freeway lane closure, while this scene is identified as an urban arterial rather than a freeway","The adjacent sidewalk is present, but its status as open, closed, or relocated is unknown"]}],"missing_scene_fields":["roadway_lane_count","work-zone limits relative to the signalized intersection","sidewalk status (open, closed, or relocated)","arrow_board_deployed and, if deployed, arrow_board_display_mode"],"selection_reason":"TA-33 is the directly applicable primary Typical Application because the scene identifies a stationary right-lane closure on a multilane divided roadway. SEC-6N.11 paragraph 06 states that when the right-hand lane is closed, TTC similar to Figure 6P-33 may be used for divided roads, and TA-33 is titled Stationary Lane Closure on a Divided Highway. The long-term duration matches the long-term treatment shown in Figure 6P-33. TA-34 was not selected because the scene provides no evidence of a temporary traffic barrier, and TA-29 was not selected as a primary or cross-reference because sidewalk closure or relocation is not established. The missing lane count does not prevent selection among the mutually exclusive primary applications: the roadway is already classified as multilane and divided, and the closed lane is identified as the right lane. Additional intersection or pedestrian treatments may be added later if the unresolved scene facts establish those conditions."}

tools.name: submit_stage2_candidate_decision_batch

instructions: SIMPLIFIED STAGE 2 — Use submit_inspection_check_batch to register a concise set of distinct, executable field checks, not a clause inventory. Keep predicates separate whenever one can fail while another passes; shared evidence or a shared inspection tool does not make them duplicates. Project-excluded scope and canonical provenance are program-enforced. After the initial compilation, call audit_stage2_candidate_coverage and review every returned predicate with submit_stage2_candidate_decision_batch. Supply exactly one structured activation, independent-violation, duplicate, action, and reason decision for every pending source node. The program binds canonical text and registers retained decisions. After the final decision batch, call the audit again. Seal only when both new_candidate_count and pending_structured_decision_count are zero. The audit is a completeness check, not an answer list or required output count. Complete all six regions and seal registration. THIS TEST MUST STOP IMMEDIATELY AFTER Stage 2 is sealed; no Stage 3 call is permitted.
